io.github.wpunit13:spark-mutation-testing-core 1.0.0 发布, Core state machine, deterministic hashing, mutation catalog and report
    writers. Pure Java 17.

    ARCHITECTURAL INVARIANT: this module must contain ZERO Spark imports.
    It has no compile- or provided-scope dependency on any org.apache.spark
    artifact, and scripts/check_no_spark_imports.sh fails the build if an
    "import org.apache.spark" statement appears in src/main/java.

    SessionResetFacade is the deliberate edge case: its logic is entirely
    Spark-specific but it is implemented purely via java.lang.reflect against
    an Object parameter, so no Spark type is ever named at compile time. That
    is why spark-sql appears below at TEST scope only: its unit test needs a
    real SparkSession to reflect against.

io.github.wpunit13:interceptor-bundle-spark-4.2_2.13 1.0.0 发布, Produces the self-contained fat jar that the Python wheel mounts via --jars,
    for Spark 4.2.x / Scala 2.13 (WP-20).

    WHY THIS BUNDLE RECOMPILES THE VERSION-AGNOSTIC LAYERS
    ------------------------------------------------------
    The 3.5 bundles ship api/dispatch/runtime classes compiled against Spark
    3.5.3. Those classes are SOURCE-identical here, but a Spark 4.2 driver
    cannot link against classes whose erased Catalyst descriptors were built
    for 3.5 when the 4.2 Catalyst signatures differ. This module therefore
    recompiles interceptor-api, interceptor-dispatch and interceptor-runtime
    FROM SOURCE (build-helper add-source) against THIS combination's Spark
    4.2.0 / Scala 2.13.18, exactly as the WP-20 spike proved possible, and
    pairs them with the 4.2-compiled shim. mutator-core is pure Java (no Spark
    imports, enforced by the CI gate) and is consumed as the reactor artifact.

    NO PACKAGE RELOCATION
    ---------------------
    Same rationale as the other bundles: relocation would rename the
    PlanMutatorShim interface named in spark.sql.extensions and break the
    ServiceLoader contract. The plugin mounts exactly one bundle per session.

    Verify after building:
      jar tf target/interceptor-spark-4.2_2.13.jar | grep -E \
        "MutatorSparkExtension|MutantRegistry|ShimImpl|META-INF/services"
    All four must be present, and the services file must be named
      META-INF/services/io.github.wpunit13.mutator.api.PlanMutatorShim
    containing the UNRELOCATED implementation class name
    (io.github.wpunit13.mutator.spark42_213.ShimImpl).

io.github.wpunit13:spark-mutation-testing-maven-plugin 1.0.0 发布, Maven plugin for Java and Scala pipelines.

    CURRENT STATUS: PLACEHOLDER. The single MutateMojo throws
    MojoExecutionException. The Java/Scala orchestration described in
    ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.4 (test-classpath introspection, matching
    shim resolution via Aether, Surefire/Failsafe argLine injection, and the
    baseline/mutation loop) is NOT implemented.

    The module exists so that:
      1. the full reactor builds and installs cleanly, and
      2. the artifact coordinate io.github.wpunit13:spark-mutation-testing-maven-plugin
         quoted in the project README actually resolves.

    Use the pytest-spark-mutation-testing Python plugin for PySpark pipelines; that
    track is complete.

io.github.wpunit13:catalyst-interceptor 1.0.0 发布, Aggregator for the Scala side of the engine. Four layers, strictly ordered:

      interceptor-api       - Spark-agnostic SPI. No concrete Catalyst types.
      interceptor-dispatch  - ServiceLoader-based runtime shim selection.
      interceptor-runtime   - SparkSessionExtensions + Rule[LogicalPlan].
      interceptor-spark-*   - One implementation per Spark/Scala combination.
      interceptor-bundle-*  - Shaded fat jar consumed by the Python wheel.

    Module order below is the dependency order and Maven honours it.
    interceptor-bundle-* is listed LAST because it packages every other
    module, so it must build after all of them.

    Note that interceptor-spark-3.5_2.13 builds BEFORE interceptor-runtime
    is tested: runtime test-depends on the shim to exercise ServiceLoader
    resolution end to end. Maven resolves this ordering automatically from
    the declared dependencies; the listing order here is documentation.

io.github.wpunit13:interceptor-bundle-spark-3.5_2.13 1.0.0 发布, Produces the single self-contained fat jar that the Python wheel mounts
    via --jars, for Spark 3.5.x / Scala 2.13.

    WHY THIS MODULE EXISTS
    ----------------------
    The pytest plugin mounts exactly ONE jar and sets
      spark.sql.extensions=io.github.wpunit13.mutator.MutatorSparkExtension
    Therefore that one jar must contain everything the driver needs:
      mutator-core          (MutantRegistry, hashing, catalog, reports and
                             SessionResetFacade, all reachable over Py4J)
      interceptor-api       (PlanMutatorShim SPI)
      interceptor-dispatch  (ShimDispatcher)
      interceptor-runtime   (MutatorSparkExtension, CatalystMutationRule)
      interceptor-spark-*   (the concrete shim + its META-INF/services entry)

    It cannot be produced by interceptor-spark-3.5_2.13 itself, because
    interceptor-runtime already test-depends on that module; having the shim
    depend on runtime would create a reactor cycle, which Maven rejects.
    A separate leaf module breaks the cycle cleanly.

    NO PACKAGE RELOCATION
    ---------------------
    Relocation is deliberately NOT used, despite the general advice in
    ARCHITECTURE.md section 5.2. Relocating io.github.wpunit13.mutator.api
    would rename the PlanMutatorShim interface that ShimImpl implements and
    that ShimDispatcher loads. Even with ServicesResourceTransformer
    Even with ServicesResourceTransformer
    rewriting the service file, the class named in
    spark.sql.extensions would also have to be the relocated name, which
    the Python plugin does not know. The net effect would be a runtime
    "no PlanMutatorShim implementation found" with no other symptom.

    Relocation exists to prevent collisions when several shim jars share a
    classpath. That cannot happen here: the plugin mounts exactly one bundle
    per session, and distinct shims live in distinct packages
    (...mutator.spark35, ...mutator.spark34) which do not collide anyway.
    When a second Spark version is added, give it its own bundle module; do
    not put two bundles on one classpath.

    Verify after building:
      jar tf target/interceptor-bundle-spark-3.5_2.13-*.jar | grep -E \
        "MutatorSparkExtension|MutantRegistry|ShimImpl|META-INF/services"
    All four must be present, and the services file must be named
      META-INF/services/io.github.wpunit13.mutator.api.PlanMutatorShim
    containing the UNRELOCATED implementation class name.

io.github.wpunit13:interceptor-bundle-spark-3.5_2.12 1.0.0 发布, Produces the self-contained fat jar that the Python wheel mounts via --jars,
    for Spark 3.5.x / Scala 2.12 (WP-19 multi-shim wheel).

    WHY A SIBLING MODULE
    --------------------
    The pytest plugin mounts exactly ONE jar; a bundle must therefore contain
    exactly ONE shim. The 2.12 shim jar carries its own 2.12-compiled copies of
    the version-agnostic api classes (the shim module recompiles them for its
    Scala binary), so bundling both shims into one jar would both duplicate the
    api classes and put two PlanMutatorShim services on one classpath — the
    exact packaging error ShimDispatcher fails loudly on. Following the
    interceptor-bundle module's own guidance ("when a second Spark version is
    added, give it its own bundle module"), this module mirrors that shade
    configuration for the 2.12 combination.

    LINKAGE STATUS (read before relying on this jar)
    ------------------------------------------------
    Resolved (was the WP-19 flagged gap): this module — like
    interceptor-bundle-4.2 — RECOMPILES the version-agnostic api, dispatch and
    runtime layers FROM SOURCE against THIS combination's Spark 3.5.3 /
    Scala 2.12.18 (build-helper add-source below), instead of shading the
    reactor's 2.13-compiled artifacts. The erased JVM descriptors of the SPI
    differ between Scala 2.12 and 2.13 (e.g. the `Seq` in
    PlanMutatorShim.classify erases to different types; ShimDispatcher's
    asScala calls bind to different helpers), so shading the reactor's 2.13
    classes produced a jar that failed to link on a 2.12-built PySpark
    (NoSuchMethodError on scala.jdk.CollectionConverters). mutator-core is
    pure Java (no Spark imports, enforced by the CI gate) and is consumed as
    the reactor artifact.

    NO PACKAGE RELOCATION
    ---------------------
    Same rationale as interceptor-bundle: relocation would rename the
    PlanMutatorShim interface named in spark.sql.extensions and break the
    ServiceLoader contract. Distinct shims live in distinct packages and the
    plugin mounts exactly one bundle per session.

    Verify after building:
      jar tf target/interceptor-spark-3.5_2.12.jar | grep -E \
        "MutatorSparkExtension|MutantRegistry|ShimImpl|META-INF/services"
    All four must be present, and the services file must be named
      META-INF/services/io.github.wpunit13.mutator.api.PlanMutatorShim
    containing the UNRELOCATED implementation class name
    (io.github.wpunit13.mutator.spark35_212.ShimImpl).
